extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard
extraction.description: A subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) for which no prior result from Srivastava et al. (2022) has outperformed the average human-rater score.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.citeAs: Suzgun, M., Scales, N., Schärli, N., Gehrmann, S., Tay, Y., Chung, H. W., Chowdhery, A., Le, Q. V., Chi, E. H., Zhou, D., & Wei, J. (2022). Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether chain-of-thought can solve them. arXiv:2210.09261.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Curated subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) for which no prior result from Srivastava et al. (2022) has outperformed the average human-rater score.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some tasks that were added later in the curation process lack human baselines, while other tasks only have the minimum number of examples needed to qualify for submission.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered BIG-Bench tasks based on criteria: tasks with more than three subtasks removed, tasks with fewer than 103 examples removed, tasks without human-rater baselines removed, tasks that do not use multiple-choice or exact match as evaluation metric removed, tasks where best reported model beats average reported human-rater score removed, extremely difficult tasks removed. For all but three tasks, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples is taken.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manually composed three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in BBH; prepended 'let's think step-by-step' to all CoT annotations in the few-shot exemplars.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Surpassing average human-rater performance score on a set of challenging tasks should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some BBH tasks require factual and general knowledge about the world as well as the common practices and presuppositions in the Western society. Ruin Names requires knowledge about human perception and usage of humor in the English language as well as the names of artists, bands, and movies in the West.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human-rater scores are not fully representative of human performance. Surpassing average human-rater performance score should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning. CoT prompting does not unlock emergent task performance in all BBH tasks.
